source: synthetic. Claude Code's tool-permission prompt, transcribed from the
        control lines the CLI renders (Allow Claude to use <Tool>? / Yes, allow
        / No, and tell Claude what to do differently) rather than captured: the
        prompt only appears for a tool this machine has not already allowed.
why: it is the permission prompt that carries none of the literals upstream's
     three permission rules are gated on — there is no "do you want to proceed?"
     and no "do you want to" anywhere on it — so upstream alone falls through to
     `osc_title_idle` and reads an unanswered prompt as a visible idle, which the
     tracker turns into a completed turn. See manifests/sidecar/claude.toml
     (`sidecar.allow_prompt_blocker`).
